name: Balancing competing goals
gist: Real problems have multiple objectives: accuracy, fairness, cost, speed. How do optimization algorithms find tradeoffs instead of optimizing just one goal?
explain: Real problems do not have one goal. A credit model must be accurate and fair—accurate so good customers get loans, but fair so it does not reject qualified applicants from certain groups, because accuracy alone will reject people unfairly. A robotic arm must be fast (complete the task soon) and safe (do not break expensive equipment), because speed without safety costs money in broken robots. A recommendation system must be accurate (show relevant items) and diverse (do not show the same kind of item every time), because boring recommendations lose users. An ML system must use little memory but still be accurate, because free memory without predictions is useless and predictions with memory costs are worthless. Making predictions faster might require less training, which hurts accuracy because the model sees fewer examples and learns less. If you optimize only for accuracy, the model may become unfair or unsafe or resource-hungry. But when you add penalties for fairness or safety, accuracy usually drops. The problem is finding a point where all goals are simultaneously reasonably good, not where one is perfect and others are ignored.

The mathematical challenge is that different goals can conflict: better fairness often means worse accuracy because enforcing fairness prevents the model from using shortcuts that help some groups, and lower cost often means slower predictions because running predictions cheaply requires simpler models or fewer computations. The space of possible tradeoffs is called the Pareto frontier—a curve where improving one goal requires sacrificing another. Finding this frontier is hard, and even after you find it, you have to choose which point on the curve to live at, which requires human judgment about what matters more.

Papers use several approaches. Multi-objective optimization methods maintain multiple candidate solutions and evolve them together, checking whether each solution improves any goal without hurting others. Others scalarize: turn multiple goals into a single combined goal by summing them with weights (e.g., 0.8 * accuracy - 0.2 * unfairness), then optimize that. The weights control which goal is most important. Some papers learn the weights adaptively—if you are doing well on fairness but poorly on speed, shift more weight toward speed. Constraint-based methods turn some goals into hard constraints (fairness must exceed a threshold) and optimize the others subject to hitting the constraint. A few papers use game theory: model the tradeoff as a negotiation between players who care about different goals. The common thread is that you do not optimize in the dark; you explicitly model what success looks like in multiple dimensions and make that tradeoff visible.

papers.title: DR-Submodular Maximization with Stochastic Biased Gradients: Classical and Quantum Gradient Algorithms
papers.contribution: Provides 1/e approximation algorithm for non-monotone DR-submodular maximization under novel constraints, surpassing the hardness result 1/4 for general convex constraints, with quantum acceleration validated numerically.

papers.title: Dual Optimistic Ascent (PI Control) is the Augmented Lagrangian Method in Disguise
papers.contribution: Establishes that dual optimistic ascent converges linearly to all local solutions with principled guidance for tuning the optimism hyperparameter.

papers.title: Efficient Submodular Maximization for Sums of Concave over Modular Functions
papers.contribution: Establishes approximation guarantees with improved query complexity; achieves up to 32.3x speedup over traditional methods on small-scale experiments.

papers.title: FAB: A First-Order AB-based Gradient Algorithm for Distributed Bilevel Optimization over Time-Varying Directed Graphs
papers.contribution: Establishes non-asymptotic convergence properties and resolves an open question about Push-Pull algorithm convergence over time-varying directed graphs; validates effectiveness on hyperparameter tuning, data hyper-cleaning, and RL.

papers.title: FIRE: Frobenius-Isometry Reinitialization for Balancing the Stability–Plasticity Tradeoff
papers.contribution: FIRE consistently outperforms naive training and standard reinitialization across continual vision learning, language modeling, and reinforcement learning domains.

papers.title: Faster Gradient Methods for Highly-smooth Stochastic Bilevel Optimization
papers.contribution: Improves upper complexity bound to Õ(p ε^-4-2/p) for p-th-order smooth problems, matching Ω(ε^-4) lower bound in highly smooth region.

papers.title: Hom-PGD$^+$: Fast Reparameterized Optimization over Non-convex Ball-Homeomorphic Set
papers.contribution: Hom-PGD+ achieves an O(ε⁻²) convergence rate to approximate stationary solutions while maintaining per-iteration complexity of only O(W) for W INN parameters, with speedups up to one order of magnitude.

papers.title: Nash Equilibria in Games with Playerwise Concave Coupling Constraints: Existence and Computation
papers.contribution: Existence of Nash equilibria is proven under playerwise concavity, and a convergent algorithm achieves epsilon-approximate constrained equilibria in O(epsilon^-3) iterations.

papers.title: A Fully First-Order Layer for Differentiable Optimization
papers.contribution: FFOLayer achieves O(log(1/epsilon)) first-order complexity for hypergradient computation and improves overall gradient complexity for constrained bilevel optimization.

papers.title: A Tale of Two Problems: Multi-Task Bilevel Learning Meets Equality Constrained Multi-Objective Optimization
papers.contribution: Proposes weighted Chebyshev penalty algorithm achieving O(ST^{-1/2}) finite-time convergence to Pareto stationarity in both deterministic and stochastic settings.

papers.title: Bilevel Optimization with Lower-Level Uniform Convexity: Theory and Algorithm
papers.contribution: Establishes novel implicit differentiation theorem and achieves O(ε^{-5p+6}) oracle complexity matching optimal rates for strongly convex functions up to log factors.

papers.title: CORAL: Uncertainty-Aware Regulation of Exposure Concentration in Recommender Systems
papers.contribution: Provides theoretical guarantees for risk bounds and finite-time recovery while achieving superior performance on real-world datasets through uncertainty-aware adaptive intervention.

papers.title: Constrained Bayesian Experimental Design via Online Planning
papers.contribution: Yields substantially more informative design sequences than existing methods across constrained BED tasks with modest computational overhead.

papers.title: Diffusion-based learning framework for Constrained Nonconvex Optimization with Weighted Bootstrapped Refinement
papers.contribution: DiOpt is the first successful diffusion solver for constrained nonconvex optimization, demonstrating superiority in both optimality and constraint satisfaction on diverse nonconvex tasks.

papers.title: Diversity-Driven Offline Multi-Objective Optimization via Nested Pareto Set Learning
papers.contribution: Finds diverse high-quality solution sets in offline MOO setting with improved robustness to surrogate errors.

papers.title: Lower Complexity Bounds for Nonconvex-Strongly-Convex Bilevel Optimization with First-Order Oracles
papers.contribution: Proves Ω(κ^{3/2}ε^{-2}) deterministic and Ω(κ^{5/2}ε^{-4}) stochastic oracle calls necessary, strengthening bounds for bilevel and min-max problems.

papers.title: OLion: Approaching the Hadamard Ideal by Intersecting Spectral and L inf Implicit Biases
papers.contribution: Matches or outperforms AdamW and Muon across large-scale language and vision training (GPT-2, Llama, SiT) while using only momentum-level optimizer state.

papers.title: Pinet: Optimizing hard-constrained neural networks with orthogonal projection layers
papers.contribution: Orders of magnitude faster training than traditional solvers on single and batch problems with superior solution quality, GPU-ready JAX implementation.

papers.title: Randomized Feasibility Methods for Constrained Optimization with Adaptive Step Sizes
papers.contribution: Achieves linear convergence in expectation for strongly convex objectives and O(1/√T) rate for nonsmooth objectives with problem parameter-free adaptive stepsizes.

papers.title: Reducing Contextual Stochastic Bilevel Optimization via Structured Function Approximation
papers.contribution: Achieves ε-stationary solution with near-optimal complexity of Õ(ε⁻³), matching best-known rate for standard SBO, with strong performance on inverse and hyperparameter optimization.

papers.title: SPREAD: Sampling-based Pareto front Refinement via Efficient Adaptive Diffusion
papers.contribution: SPREAD matches or exceeds leading baselines in efficiency, scalability, and Pareto front coverage across multi-objective optimization benchmarks.

papers.title: Solving Imperfect-Recall Games via Sum-of-Squares Optimization
papers.contribution: Proves asymptotic convergence with finite convergence under genericity, and identifies (SOS)-concave/(SOS)-monotone classes with first-level convergence via single SDP.

papers.title: Task-Agnostic Amortized Multi-Objective Optimization
papers.contribution: TAMO reduces proposal time by 50-1000x versus alternatives while matching or improving Pareto quality under tight evaluation budgets.

papers.title: The Pareto-optimal Trade-off between Regret and Statistical Inference in Linear Stochastic Bandits under Safety Constraints
papers.contribution: The paper achieves optimal trade-offs along the Pareto frontier between regret, parameter estimation, and safety with near-constant safety risk.

papers.title: The Theory and Practice of MAP Inference over Non-Convex Constraints
papers.contribution: Structure-aware approach outperforms constraint-agnostic baselines on synthetic and real-world benchmarks for constrained MAP inference.

papers.title: Towards Safe and Optimal Online Bidding: A Modular Look-ahead Lyapunov Framework
papers.contribution: Provides adaptive guarantees with optimal regret and constraint violation bounds that match or improve best-known results across multiple auction settings.
